title: Small perfect classes containing an arbitrary small family in D(A)
statement: Let A be a Grothendieck abelian category with Hom and derived-Hom universe v [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every essentially v-small class P in D(A), there exists an essentially v-small replete triangulated class S containing P, perfect in the sense that componentwise surjectivity on Hom from S survives all v-small coproducts. Moreover, for every v-small family Y_i in S and every map f:U to coproduct Y_i with U in S, there are a v-small type J, a map a:J to I, and a factorization of f through coproduct_j Y_(a j), with that subcoproduct itself in S.

source.place: Ambient well-generation and common cardinal bound: Neeman Theorem 0.2; Krause Localization theory Sections 6.2-6.3 and Proposition 6.8.1.

proof.text: Apply the well-generation core theorem to obtain an essentially small replete triangulated class S containing P, together with a common regular cardinal alpha, alpha-presentability of every object of S, and closure under coproducts indexed by types of cardinality less than alpha.

Use the alpha-presentability and the small-coproduct closure to obtain componentwise surjectivity after coproducts and factorization through a subcoproduct; these are the formal cardinal-smallness consequences of Krause Proposition 6.8.1.
Package the two conclusions with the properties of S and the inclusion P <= S.

lean.statement:
theorem derived_exists_perfectSmallClass
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{v} A]
    (P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory A))
    [ObjectProperty.EssentiallySmall.{v} P] :
    ∃ S : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory A),
      ObjectProperty.EssentiallySmall.{v} S ∧ S.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧
      S.IsTriangulated ∧ P ≤ S ∧
      (∀ (I : Type v) (X Y : I → DerivedCategory A) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ Y i),
        (∀ i U, S U → Function.Surjective (fun g : U ⟶ X i ↦ g ≫ f i)) →
        ∀ U, S U → Function.Surjective
          (fun g : U ⟶ ∐ X ↦ g ≫ Limits.Sigma.map f)) ∧
      (∀ (I : Type v) (Y : I → DerivedCategory A), (∀ i, S (Y i)) →
        ∀ (U : DerivedCategory A), S U → ∀ f : U ⟶ ∐ Y,
        ∃ (J : Type v) (a : J → I), S (∐ fun j ↦ Y (a j)) ∧
          ∃ g : U ⟶ ∐ fun j ↦ Y (a j),
            g ≫ Sigma.desc (fun j ↦ Sigma.ι Y (a j)) = f)
